info.title: Brigade API
info.description:
Brigade's public HTTP API: what an integration may call. Everything else (incidents, monitors,
schedules, escalation policies, devices) is read and changed over Brigade Sync, the WebSocket `openSync` opens
(RFC 0004). Routes not listed here are internal and may change without notice.

**Auth.** A Better Auth session: sign in with `POST /api/auth/sign-in/email` (`{ "email", "password" }`) and send
the cookie it sets. Writes that carry a cookie refuse another site's `Origin` (`403 forbidden_origin`); a request
without `Origin` is not refused for it. API tokens do not exist yet (see RFC 0002 "Public HTTP API").

**Errors.** Every refusal is JSON, `{ "error": "<code>" }`, with the codes each operation lists. Any other method on
a listed path answers `405` with `Allow`; an unknown path `404 not_found`.

**Webhooks.** What Brigade sends to the endpoints a workspace registers: a signed `POST` per event, as the Standard
Webhooks specification has it (`@freecorps/brigade-sdk`'s `verifyWebhook`, or any of its libraries, verifies
it). Each payload is `version: 1`; fields may be added to it, so ignore the ones you do not know. A change that
is not purely additive is a new version. See RFC 0005 "Outbound webhooks".

servers.description: A Brigade deployment: the dashboard's origin, under /api.

get.description: `HEAD` answers the same without a body.

get.summary: Whether the paging pipeline proved itself lately
get.description: Without a session, or for a user in no workspace, only `status`. A member of any workspace also gets the reasons and times, since a responder needs to know they may not be paged.

post.description: The token is the monitor's heartbeat URL's last segment (shown once, when the monitor is made or its URL rotated): it names the workspace and the monitor and carries the secret. The body is never read. Every refusal is the same `404`, so a wrong secret looks like a missing monitor.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: `<workspaceId>.<monitorId>.<secret>`, from the monitor's heartbeat URL.

post.description: The signed-in user becomes its owner, and it becomes the session's active workspace. Bodies over 4 KiB are refused. A `400` for a bad name lists the problems in `issues`.

403.description: Refused: another site's `Origin`, not a member, or not allowed.

patch.description: Owners and admins, by the rules of RFC 0003 "Members". `409 conflict`: the members changed meanwhile, reload and retry. `503 not_applied`: the change is made and the workspace is catching up; sending it again finishes it sooner.

parameters.name: workspaceId
parameters.description: The workspace (`ws_<ULID>`).

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: The member's user id (`usr_<ULID>`); your own to leave.

403.description: Refused: another site's `Origin`, not a member, or not allowed.

delete.description: Removes the member and their devices; with your own user id, leaves the workspace. `409 last_owner`: a workspace keeps at least one owner.

parameters.name: workspaceId
parameters.description: The workspace (`ws_<ULID>`).

parameters.description: The member's user id (`usr_<ULID>`); your own to leave.

post.description: Owners and admins, with a verified address; an admin cannot invite an owner. Brigade emails the invitation. Limited per workspace, inviter and address (`429`, or `409 send_limit` past the workspace's daily cap).

get.description: The workspace, and whether it can still be accepted. Who invited and the role only when the invitation is for the signed-in address (`forYou`); never the address itself.

parameters.description: The invitation (`inv_<ULID>`), as in the link its email carries.

parameters.description: Your id for this ack, so a retry after a lost answer runs it once.

get.description: Incidents, monitors, schedules and the rest are read and changed over Brigade Sync (RFC 0004), not REST: this upgrade opens it, as the signed-in member. The frames are not modeled here; see `@freecorps/brigade-sync/protocol`.

parameters.description: The workspace (`ws_<ULID>`).

parameters.name: webhook-id
parameters.description: The event's id (`evt_<ULID>`), the payload's `id`: the same on every retry, so de-duplicate by it.

parameters.name: webhook-timestamp
parameters.description: When this attempt was signed, Unix seconds. Refuse one more than 5 minutes off.

parameters.name: webhook-signature
parameters.description: `v1,<base64 HMAC-SHA256>` of `<webhook-id>.<webhook-timestamp>.<body>` under each secret in use (two while one is rotated), space separated. The key is the secret's bytes after `whsec_`, base64-decoded.

2XX.description: Received. Anything else, or no answer in 5 s, is retried.
